second_order: working out which April Fools jokes work
theme_note: These codes judge, expose, defend, repair, or give advice about jokes; what varies is whether believability, harmlessness, effort, or timing is treated as the test.

second_order: making fake Nintendo announcements and April Fools bits
theme_note: These passages make or extend the room's own false releases, cancellations, acquisitions, advertisements, reviews, and comedy pieces; they vary from improvised replies to moderator-produced podcast material.

second_order: keeping regular posting places and rules in force on April Fools
theme_note: These codes establish Showoff Saturday as real and recurring, redirect a purchase post there, accept that routing, and apply the text-post rule to a joke image; the shared practice is maintaining ordinary content arrangements during the joke day.

second_order: avoiding giving a piracy video views while sharing its gist
theme_note: One exchange coordinates not clicking a piracy video, asks for a summary instead, supplies that summary, and resists overgeneralising from its uploader.

second_order: calling people to make Nintendo marks on the canvas
theme_note: These codes recruit builders, provide coordinates or templates, show placements, share drawings, and ask for help with Mario, Pikmin, Samus, Switch, Game Boy, Contra, Gradius, Peach, and other marks; the target varies while the mobilising practice holds.

second_order: reporting what survives, changes, or fails on the canvas
theme_note: These codes tell the room that pixels were erased, space was defended, attempts lacked traction, sprites vanished or transformed, and one larger logo failed while the original survived; later the finished portrait is read for Nintendo visibility.

second_order: working out the target, location, name, and plan
theme_note: These passages counsel starting smaller, reject already-held ground, correct sprite names, request links or coordinates, flag conflicting colours, and choose another builder's plan; what varies is the unresolved detail being settled.

second_order: dealing with other canvas groups as allies, opponents, or claimants
theme_note: These codes contest Blue Corner, propose joining Red Corner, propose altering PCMasterRace or OSU, answer outside requests, and ask for help against r/india; relations vary among alliance, attack, defence, and competing claims.

second_order: repairing and defending Nintendo marks under attack
theme_note: These codes call for help under attack, spend time fixing logos, keep them clean, join and honour defenders, call for rebuilding, and later ask to rebuild Samus or save Kerby.

second_order: sending separate r/place posts back to Operation Mario
theme_note: These exchanges redirect satellite sprite and help posts to the active megathread, sometimes including requests for the link, provision of it, and thanks; the proposed figures change but the centralising practice repeats.

second_order: pushing back on r/place posts and requests
theme_note: These comments call a logo a waste of time, defend participation as fun, complain about thread spam, refuse an obligation to help, and challenge the tone of a request; the pushback ranges from venue fatigue to interpersonal refusal.

second_order: keeping a non-Nintendo sprite outside r/nintendo
theme_note: This single code records the moderator removing a Contra r/place sprite because it was not directly about Nintendo; it belongs with no other live code closely enough to widen the practice.

second_order: handling r/place posts after the canvas closed
theme_note: These codes close a new Peach proposal because r/place ended, then remove, contest, reclassify, and route a retrospective finished-canvas image as fan art; the variation is between stopping new action and placing retrospective material.

second_order: asking for upvotes for Roy in blue
theme_note: This single surviving title seeks attention for a Roy canvas image and does not show a build request, plan negotiation, or repair exchange that would justify placing it elsewhere.
